 KLAS Las Vegas Follow Las Vegas man sentenced for $5M tax refund fraud scheme
 Jay Adkins Wed, October 21, 2026 at 10:49 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. LAS VEGAS ( KLAS ) -- A Las Vegas man was sentenced Wednesday to 38 months in prison for conspiring to defraud the United States by filing false tax returns with the IRS and diverting portions of the resulting tax refunds to himself and his co-defendant.
  >>Download the free 8 News+ app for live newscasts and streaming originals   
 According to court documents and statements made in court, Ivan Odiaga prepared federal income tax returns at Silver State Tax & Multiservices LLC, a tax preparation business in Las Vegas owned by his mother and co-defendant, Iris Hondermann. From 2017 through 2021, Odiaga and his mother prepared tax returns for clients that included one or more false items, including business profits and losses, COVID-19 sick and family leave credits, and residential energy credits.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In 2020 and 2021, Odiaga prepared some of these returns using the Preparer Tax Identification Number of another tax preparer without permission, according to documents.
 Between 2017 and 2021, Odiaga and his mother prepared false tax returns filed with the IRS seeking more than $5 million in refunds that their clients were not entitled to receive. At times, Odiaga and his mother also diverted portions of client tax refunds to themselves. From 2017 through 2021, they diverted more than $1.1 million in fraudulent tax refunds to bank accounts one or both of them controlled.
 Hondermann previously pleaded guilty to one count of conspiring to defraud the United States.
 Quotes
 "This office has zero tolerance for corrupt tax professionals who treat the U.S. Treasury like their personal slush fund and prey on innocent taxpayers," said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. "The defendant abused a position of trust to orchestrate a brazen, multi-million dollar theft. Today's sentence makes it crystal clear: If you scheme to defraud the government and steal from your clients, we will hunt you down, dismantle your operation, and ensure you face hard time in federal prison."
 Advertisement Advertisement "Mr. Odiaga's federal prison sentence sends a clear message that tax professionals who abuse their position of trust and steal from taxpayers are being held accountable," said IRS Criminal Investigation San Francisco Field Office Acting Special Agent in Charge John Abram. "For years, the defendant and his mother used fraud and deception to exploit hundreds of clients and enrich themselves at the expense of the American taxpayer. IRS Criminal Investigation will continue to pursue those who feed their greed and threaten the integrity of our tax system."
